scaled_small_mapf.description: Scaled congested MAPF (narrow corridors with passing pockets, four-way crossings, dense random 8x8/9x9 grids) at the tight per-tick planning budget. Reproduces the central Fig. 2 claim: a bounded real-time planner keeps full-horizon success, a planner that restarts its search every tick does not, and tight budgets cost solution quality.
scaled_small_mapf.notes: The paper reports Fig. 2 graphically. success_rate keeps the qualitative targets recorded by the original reproduction (real-time = full-horizon = 1.0, restart far lower). The paper reports no number for realtime_score, mean_log_normalized_cost or mean_log_planning_work; those entries are this gym's scaled-reproduction values (20 evaluator-built instances, budget 1000 metered events per tick, cumulative cap 2,000,000) in place of millisecond cutoffs and the 60 s timeout. Reproduced held-out success_rate under the same cumulative work cap: full_lacam 0.850, naive_rt_lacam 0.300, rt_lacam 0.750.

realtime_score.description: Mean over evaluator-built instances of a per-instance score in [0, 1]: 0 if the executed joint path is illegal, misses the goals, or runs out of ticks or cumulative planning work; otherwise 1 - log10(cost / lower bound) / log10(worst cost the tick horizon allows / lower bound). Cost is the sum of costs of the path the evaluator executed, including waits charged for decisions that exceeded the per-tick planning budget.

success_rate.description: Fraction of instances whose evaluator-executed path is legal and reaches all goals within the tick horizon and the cumulative planning-work cap.

mean_log_normalized_cost.description: Mean log10 of sum-of-costs divided by the sum of individual shortest-path lengths (the paper's normalized cost, on the log axis the paper plots); failed instances count as the worst cost the tick horizon allows.

mean_log_planning_work.description: Mean log10(1 + W / 1000), where W is the evaluator-metered planning work (executed Python line and call events) summed over all ticks of an episode -- the hardware-independent analogue of the paper's total planning time; failed instances count as the cumulative work cap, as the paper counts timed-out runs at the timeout.

scaled_small_mapf_budget3.description: The same scaled instances at a three-times larger per-tick budget: success parity should hold, and solution quality should improve with the larger cutoff, as in the paper's cutoff sweep.
scaled_small_mapf_budget3.notes: Same provenance as scaled_small_mapf; per-tick budget 3000 metered events, same cumulative cap (the paper keeps one 60 s cap across cutoffs). Reproduced held-out success_rate under the same cumulative work cap: full_lacam 0.850, naive_rt_lacam 0.300, rt_lacam 0.800.

movingai_random32.description: MovingAI MAPF benchmark map random-32-32-20 (the paper's Fig. 2 map) with 6-12 agents placed at random free cells, tight per-tick budget. Real-time planning should match full-horizon success while restart replanning fails more often.
movingai_random32.notes: Formerly movingai_random32_4agent (three public 4-agent scenarios that were also downloadable answers). success_rate keeps the recorded targets of that experiment (1.0 / 1.0 / 0.667). The paper uses 25 scenes per map and up to 400 agents; this gym uses 16 evaluator-sampled instances with 6-12 agents (pure-Python planners), budget 3000 metered events per tick and a cumulative cap of 6,000,000. Values of the other metrics are scaled-reproduction values. Reproduced held-out success_rate under the same cumulative work cap: full_lacam 0.875, naive_rt_lacam 0.562, rt_lacam 0.875.
